Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1295eb7c33b9bb1714f0c71ffb2a47f767c78a56`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-project/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json, skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md + packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: yes

Readings below are against `main` at `de395b42` and the PR head above, read through git objects only. Card #35345 with all six comments, PR #35572 (body, 11 files, net diff) and the head's check-runs were the inputs; the rulings and source files the diff cites were read to judge it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Schema accept set: unchanged — right.** Nothing under `packages/spec/src/**` moves; the generator only imports `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE`, `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES`, `ValueDomainSchema`, `VALUE_DOMAIN_FIELD_NAMES`, `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS`, `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` and `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES`.
- **Published surface: `@objectstack/skills` gains one file and three text changes — right as a set, wrong in two claims (M1, M2).** New `references/platform-catalog.md`; §0 question 3 and §5 step 4 in `objectstack-project/SKILL.md`; one sentence in `field-types.md`; six eval fixtures. A new published convention rides with it, the `// PLATFORM-CANDIDATE:` marker, which the card rules.
- **The catalog is generated, deterministic and gated — right.** `renderPlatformCatalog()` is a pure function of constants (array order and insertion order only, no clock, no directory listing). It is emitted through the same sink as the `_index.md` files, so `check:skill-refs` (in the required `TypeScript Type Check` job) reds on a missing, stale or hand-edited page, and `catalogProblems()` fails the run before emit when a row names an object, token or domain the spec does not declare. `platform-catalog.test.ts` pins the names, exhaustiveness and byte-identical re-render.
- **What is derived and what is not.** Derived from the spec: object names, the "Mounted by" column, value-domain names and field-name lists, capability tokens, edition, boot. Written by hand in `lib/platform-catalog.ts`: which 30 objects are listed, both prose columns, the 32 capability descriptions, every intro paragraph, the "Not owned" and "Planned" rows. The guards check names; no gate can check the prose, and that is where M1, M2 and N1 sit.
- **Governance register: the `spec-skill-refs` candidate now also admits `references/platform-catalog.md` under any skill — the gate still holds.** Read as a gate edit, as claim amendment 7012111198 asks. It widens which paths may be asked the lift question, so it narrows what the gate holds by one filename and nothing else; the answer is still the generator's own proof, per file, as before. No route was found by which a hand-written change to the page lands outside the governed path. The basis of that judgment went to the dispatching seat with this record and is not restated here. See S2 and escalation 2 in ③.
- **Is the regexp pinned: indirectly.** `check-governed-merges --self-test` has no case naming the catalog (`REGISTER_SAMPLES` holds one `_index.md`; the live battery asserts only that sample is in the manifest). The pin is the ratchet's tripwire: `check-skills-token-ratchet --self-test` asserts the excluded set by name through `generatedExceptionFor()`, so reverting the regexp, or widening it onto an existing hand-authored file, reds there. N5.
- **Token ratchet: excluded set +1 path, one ceiling row `2901 → 2990`.** Recomputed from the blobs: `SKILL.md` is 11619 bytes on `main` (2900 priced tokens) and 11977 on the head (2990), stamp line 20 bytes both sides; `field-types.md` 14210 → 14205 bytes (3553 → 3552, row untouched at 3553). The raise is right under the standing path; its recorded authority is wrong (S1). The exclusion is right mechanically and wrong in class (S2).
- **Check-runs at the head:** 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. `Lint UI` is skipped.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills: patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, both lines present in the PR body and the changeset. This matches the diff: it publishes teaching text and a reference page from `skills/` and nothing else. `packages/spec` ships `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `src/**/*.zod.ts` and its ledgers, never `scripts/`, so no `@objectstack/spec` changeset is owed. `Check Changeset` is green. The `Clause-②: no` line is right: no accept set widens or narrows.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag (a), the ceiling raise.** Answered: the standing path of ruling record 6513306068 (part 2) allows it without a per-card ruling, and its form is met — same-file deletions are in the diff, the PR body quotes 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」 and names the record, the measured delta (+89) is in the body, and the row is pinned at the measurement (2990/2990). Two qualifications: the second citation is wrong (S1), and one of the two cuts is not a pure restatement (N3). The dispatch order asked for the bytes to be paid in full, and claim amendment 7012111198 names the ratchet file for the excluded-path line only; accepting this further edit of the same file is the dispatching seat's call. **Escalated to the seat.**
- **Dev flag (b), the branch.** `claude/project-thread-1d1bw6` matches claim amendment 7011960871. No action.
- **`open_questions`:** none in report 7014293667.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`:** two `ui/scripts` test files fail on a box without a `ui` build ("ran no case at all"). `Test UI` is green at the head, so it is not this PR's. The shape is a red where the repo's convention is exit 3, prerequisite not met; the seat may file that as its own card.
- **Escalation 1, the card's ruling record.** Card #35345's body says the maintainer's 「同意」 at 05:46Z answered the skills analysis. Record 7000955097 on #35328 attributes the 「同意」 of 05:46:53Z to "the five-point recommendation" on cross-suite linkage, and nothing on #35328 or #35345 records a ruling on the skills scope. The scope reads as ruled only through the card body. The seat should confirm from the project thread and post the record on #35345.
- **Escalation 2, the reach of the generated-file carve-out.** The #11705 ruling the register quotes rests on "no agent-authored instruction content can enter through them". After this PR the same generator carries hand-written instruction prose into `skills/**`. The gate still holds such a change (①), but the extension of that row, and of the ratchet's excluded population, to a page with hand-written text rests on claim amendment 7012111198, which is a seat's line and not a ruling. This PR lands on the Tier H path either way; the maintainer should be told this is in it.
- **Why the security line reads yes.** The catalog's people, history and sharing rows, its capability table and eval 9 teach permission, sharing and sign-in behaviour that the path names do not show. The adopting seat adds the `security` label.
- **SQL push-down:** not applicable — the diff adds no query, id materialisation or join.
- **PR body against the tree:** the body says the ratchet self-test's subtotal pin shifts by 89; the diff has no such hunk (two hunks: the row and the excluded path). The body gives the catalog as 2560 tokens; the blob is 10244 bytes, 2561. Neither changes a judgment.

### ④ Design judgment

**The PR delivers every item of the card's scope in form: the generated catalog with its three tables, the "Not owned" rows, a capped "Planned" section, §0 question 3 and the §5 sweep kept apart from §3, the `valueDomain` sentence, and three evals per skill. It fails on two statements of platform behaviour that `main` does not have.**

M1 (must-fix) — **the catalog and eval 23 say forms and filters pick a value-domain field from the standard; on `main` only the currency code does.** `lib/platform-catalog.ts` writes, and the page publishes: "the write path refuses a non-member, and Setup, forms and filters pick from the standard." Eval 23 in `objects-fields-relationships.json` expects "the forms pick from it, so there is no picklist of countries to maintain". On `main`, `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/TextField.tsx` swaps in a picker only when `isCurrencyCodeField` holds (`valueDomain` equal to `iso_4217_currency`); a `text` field declaring `iana_time_zone` or `iso_3166_alpha2` renders the plain input, and no list or filter component reads `valueDomain` at all. The settings page's `DomainCombobox` serves settings specifiers, not object fields. The write refusal is real (`value_domain`), and so is the `os lint` warning (`field/missing-value-domain`, text fields only). Trim the sentence and the eval to what is delivered. `field-types.md` itself asserts only the refusal and stands; its "never a free-text or picklist copy" then leaves a user typing `CN` into a text box, and the seat should decide whether that absolute survives once its stated reason is gone — the lint rule does not warn on a `select` named `country`.

M2 (must-fix) — **the `sys_mailbox` row sends the author to a door that does not exist.** Its reach cell reads "Setup declares mailboxes; data API read". On `main` the object is `managedBy: 'engine-owned'` and read-only over the data API, served to mailbox administrators only; no Setup navigation entry names it; no non-test code inserts a row. The package README states that `requires: ['mailbox']` mounts the objects and the ingest seam and syncs no mailbox, and that mail arrives only where the host composes `MailboxServicePlugin` with an IMAP account source. The card's own condition for a row is "confirm an app can actually look the object up or write it". Rewrite the cell from the object and the README, and say on the `sys_mail_message` row where mail comes from, or drop the row.

S1 (should-fix) — **the ceiling row cites a record that does not say what it is cited for.** The comment on the `skills/objectstack-project/SKILL.md` row, and the PR body, name ruling record 7000955097 as "the ruling of record that orders this text into the file". That record is the cross-suite linkage ruling: owner system per entity, no sync now, reuse of `srm_material`, the freeze list, units. It names no skill, no §0, no §5. The raise does not need it — record 6513306068 authorises the measured remainder on its own form, which is met. Correct the row comment to cite the standing path as the authority and the card as the scope, so the gate's source does not carry a precedent for "a ruling orders this text" that no record supports.

S2 (should-fix) — **2561 tokens of hand-written teaching text are now priced by nothing.** The ratchet excludes generator-owned files because "the generated bytes are a function of the schema source", so the author who could pay is not the one the red lands on. That is false for this page: its rows, descriptions and paragraphs are written in `lib/platform-catalog.ts`, and that author can pay by deleting text. §0 tells every project to read the page before adding an object, a field or a flow, so it is customer context. As classified, any later PR can lengthen the prose with no ceiling and no ruling, which is the growth the 10402 ruling was made to stop. The card rules the catalog's existence and size, not its exemption. Either pin a shrink-only ceiling on the hand-written text in `platform-catalog.test.ts`, or carry a ruling that says the exemption is intended.

S3 (should-fix) — **eval 22 teaches an interim unit field that the linked contract will make the app migrate.** Its expected output builds "a `select` field whose options are the units this business uses" for the prompt's "pcs, kg, box". ADR-0158, which the Planned row links as the contract, fixes UN/ECE Rec 20 codes in exact uppercase (`KGM`; the piece code is `H87`), and item 5 of record 7000955097 orders the same for `uom` so that the platform list later "adds validation only and leaves stored values unchanged". An app that stores `kg` and `pcs` gets the data migration the card exists to prevent. The expected output should store the contract's codes as the option values, with the business's spellings as labels.

S4 (should-fix) — **the cut that pays for the new sentence removes the only place the data skill shows where `homeAmount` is written.** The deleted comment was the one literal with `homeAmount` nested inside `currencyConfig` and its three keys taking field names. What remains names the key and its three members in prose and never says it sits under `currencyConfig`; the only statement of that left in the bundle is the catalog cell, in another skill. Eval 24, added in this PR, expects exactly that shape. The PR body calls the cut "restated elsewhere in the rule"; the second cut is, this one is not. Write the prose as `currencyConfig.homeAmount`, or restore the nesting another way.

N1 (nit) — `sys_user_position` reach reads "positions the app's permission sets grant". Positions distribute permission sets (ADR-0090: capability is the set, distribution is the position), so the cell reads inverted. It came from the role-word reword at `1295eb7c`.

N2 (nit) — question 3 now sits between question 2 and the "Default to own use" paragraph that belongs to it. And an MCP-only build, which applies only §0 and §3, is told to mark its own build with a `//` comment it has no file for, and §5's sweep does not apply to it. The card's ruled wording is followed; a follow-up card can say where an MCP-only build records the candidate.

N3 (nit) — the cut "Unsure whether a check exists? Inject the defect and run the command" is not a pure restatement. The technique survives in §2's retire sentence, for a rule that has landed; the use for an author who does not know whether a check exists is gone, and no eval covers it.

N4 (nit) — "Mounted by" falls back to "every boot" for any package that backs no capability token. That is true of `platform-objects`; `plugin-security` is mounted by the auth-tier pairing in `serve`; it would be false for `cloud-connection` or `metadata-core` if a row from either were added. In the other direction, `requires: ['audit']` and "on `requires`" understate a stock boot: the default preset opens `auth`, `ui` and `i18n`, `serve` pairs `AuditPlugin` with auth, and `mcp` is a host default. Declaring the token is harmless, so no reader is led wrong.

N5 (nit) — the register row's `what` text, the #11705 header section and the ratchet's population 2 paragraph still describe only schema indexes and "not hand-authored skill content", and `check-governed-merges --self-test` has no case that names the catalog path or a near miss beside it.

N6 (nit) — the "Not owned" party row gives "(tax id, email)" as key examples. The ruled keys are country plus credit code or registration number for parties, and material number and plant code for items.

N7 (nit) — data evals 22 and 24 score `objectstack-data` on behaviour only `objectstack-project` teaches: the catalog lookup, the marker, `sys_exchange_rate`. Nothing in `skills/objectstack-data` outside the evals points at the catalog, so a session that loads only the data skill on "add a `uom` text field" meets nothing that asks question 3. That is the card's reach, not this PR's defect: a follow-up card for a one-line pointer from the domain skills.

Checked and holding: every other object row's reach against its own `enable` block and routes on `main` (`apiMethods` or its absence for all 30; `enable.files` default off, `feeds` and `activities` default on; the recycle-bin restore route; the import-jobs route; the approvals routes; `sharingRules`, `queues`, `assignmentRules`, `webhooks` and `emailTemplates` as stack keys; Setup entries for exchange rates, sharing rules, queues and assignment rules; `mailAssociation` live in the liveness ledger; `view_all_audit_log` in the capability registry); the value-domain field-name lists; all 32 capability rows against the token list, providers and always-on slate; both Planned links (ADR-0158 is on `main`, #35340 is open).

Delta review d1 of the FAIL record 7015659227. Read through git objects only: the interdiff from `1295eb7c` to the head above, the head's blobs, and `main` at `f981dce3`. The fix-round accounts (7016714878, 7016751165) and the PR body were read and then set aside; every line below is from the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moved.** One commit on top of `1295eb7c`, eight files, +191/−65. No merge of `main` in the fix round; the branch's one merge is the pre-PR one already in the first head, and the merge-base is still `c890070f`. `main` has moved 18 commits since and none touches a path this PR reads or writes (the spec registries, the text widget, the mailbox service, `packages/spec/scripts`, both gate scripts, `skills/**`). Untouched since the first round: the changeset, `build-skill-references.ts`, `project-process.json`.
- **Every hunk maps to a named item, with one unnamed reword.** `lib/platform-catalog.ts`: the value-domain paragraph (M1), the two mail rows (M2), the position row (N1), the two master-data rows (N6), the paragraphs hoisted into `PROSE` and `handWrittenBytes()` (S2). `platform-catalog.test.ts`: the pricing leg (S2). `check-governed-merges.mjs`: two self-test cases and the battery floor 23 to 25 (N5); no register row, rule or regexp moved. `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: comment lines of one row only; no executable line and no number moved (S1). The catalog page: the regenerated bytes of the above, and `check:skill-refs` is green on the head.
- **M1 in the tree.** The paragraph now reads: the write path refuses a non-member; forms pick the currency code from ISO 4217; a time zone or a country is typed into a plain text input; no list or filter reads the domain. Record 7000955097 is cited nowhere in the tree or the body. This agrees with the ruling-source record 7016042622 on the card.
- **S2 in the tree.** Summed from the blob: the strings `handWrittenBytes()` counts are 6331 bytes, 1583 tokens in the ratchet's measure, and the test's ceiling is 1583, pinned at the measurement. ### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the first round: `@objectstack/skills` patch, by the changeset already on the branch. Nothing under `packages/spec/src/**` moved and `packages/spec` does not ship `scripts/`, so no spec changeset is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The PR body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; both still fit the tree.
- **For the seat: the new ceiling names its own raise path.** The pricing leg's comment says a later raise of the 1583 ceiling follows the ratchet header's path under the standing ruling. Record 6513306068 recognises that path for the ratchet's rows; it does not name a ceiling held in a test file. Adopting it here is reasonable and is what S2 asked for, but recognising it is the seat's call, not the area's or this record's.
- The first round's two escalations (the further edit of the ratchet file beyond claim amendment 7012111198, and the classification of the page as generator-owned) are not reopened by this round; S2's pricing leg answers the second in substance.
- The PR body is behind the tree in two places (it describes the field-types sentence in its first-round wording, and calls the N2 move "zero bytes"). The tree is the record.

### ④ Design judgment

S5 (should-fix) — **eval 22 now hard-asserts `H87` and `KGM`, and no file under `skills/` says either.** The codes are reachable only through the Planned row's link to ADR-0158. The catalog's Planned paragraph tells the author to "build its own meanwhile", marked with the link; nothing tells them to build it on the linked contract's keys. So an author who follows the skill as written still stores `kg` and `pcs` and gets the migration S3 named, and an eval session that cannot open the link cannot pass the two literals. Either add the clause to the Planned paragraph (for example "on the linked contract's codes, so the swap leaves stored values unchanged", paid inside the 1583 ceiling), or keep the codes in `expected_output` and drop them from `must_contain`. Not blocking: the expected output itself is now right.
